newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil pulled higher by futures, firm premium.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil pulled higher by futures, firm premium.

text.p: NWE gas oil was knocked higher by stronger futures and firm premiums.
May IPE gas oil was $1.25 a tonne stronger at $166.50 at 1130 GMT, pulled higher by crude futures bolstered by technical factors and Bonny force majeure by Shell Nigeria.

Diesel cargoes continued to attract strong premiums because of supply tightness with the market hovering around May IPE +$11 cif NWE. Talk was ongoing, but nothing was though concluded in the morning.

Russian heating oil was quiet after a recent busy period when small parcels went into the ARA market, traders said. Demand for large cargoes to take to Asia continued to underpin the NWE gas oil market.
"The Asian draw is the key to keeping ARA from being flooded," said one trader at a major. Russian was pegged around May IPE +$2 cif NWE.
DIN and FOD were only thinly talked around May IPE +$4-5 cif.
Heating oil barges were heard offered around May IPE +$1.25 fob, but buying interest was almost non-existent, particularly for second half April material.

"The low water level may have something to do with this, people say freight is high," said one barge trader who thought the stronger numbers on the back of the futures may also be putting some buying interest off.
